topIssues.title: flaky test: `XDM_MinGasLimits_Succeeds::invariant_minGasLimits`
topIssues.author: maurelian
topIssues.body:
https://app.circleci.com/pipelines/workflows/c9c37921-2268-4b12-a541-8034abfb303c (job `contracts-bedrock-tests-develop BRIDGE_HOOK`, [5757143](https://circleci.com/gh/ethereum-optimism/optimism/5757143))

Fails in about 1 in 6 `contracts-bedrock-tests-develop` jobs since #23619, which builds the contracts once and shares `cache/`, `artifacts/` and `forge-artifacts/` with the test jobs through the workspace. It did not fail before that change. It does not reproduce locally, and rerunning with the same `FOUNDRY_FUZZ_SEED` passes.

Every failure is a `relay` call with `value=1` that reverts with empty data ([`CrossDomainMessenger.t.sol#L84`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/bb389124e2da8aa1ddce029e29c3ca01bb40317a/packages/contracts-bedrock/test/invariants/CrossDomainMessenger.t.sol#L84)). Diagnostics on #23638 show the cause. When the relay reverts, the portal and `0x04` both have balance 0, although `setUp` deals the portal `type(uint128).max` ([L108](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/bb389124e2da8aa1ddce029e29c3ca01bb40317a/packages/contracts-bedrock/test/invariants/CrossDomainMessenger.t.sol#L108)) and 1 to 7 earlier value relays in the same run succeeded:

```
DIAG value=1 data=0x opBalance=0 idBalance=0 valueRelays=2
```

The balances drop to zero mid-run, but code and storage survive. That points to forge (1.8.3-dev) rather than the contracts.

A/B test on #23638:

| Arm | Failures |
|---|---|
| Shared build, default invariant workers | 5 of 24 |
| Shared build, `FOUNDRY_INVARIANT_WORKERS=1` | 1 of 6 |
| Compile in the test job (as before #23619) | 0 of 18 |

🤖 *Co-created with Claude Opus 5.5*

topPRs.title: kona-engine: share engine task steps instead of running tasks from tasks
topPRs.author: joshklop
topPRs.body:
Engine tasks reused each other's steps by constructing and executing other tasks. `InsertTask`, `ConsolidateTask`, `FinalizeTask` and `Engine::reset` each built a `SynchronizeTask` only to execute it, `SealTask` executed an `InsertTask`, and `ConsolidateTask`'s fallback executed a `BuildTask` and a `SealTask` in an "atomic" mode. On a Holocene invalid payload, `SealTask` called back into that fallback, so the two recursed into each other. The shared steps are now plain functions that the tasks call, and only the engine's queue executes tasks. Each queued task is a flat sequence of steps, and `SealTask` no longer needs a flag to tell it which caller it is serving.

Operators see no change in behavior. The derived-block path no longer logs "Starting new seal job", and a successful Holocene deposits-only replacement now logs the block it imported.

The `kona-engine` public API loses `SynchronizeTask` and `BuildSealCoupling`, and `SealTask::new` loses its `is_attributes_derived` and `coupling` arguments. Nothing else in the monorepo uses them.

Fourth PR in the stack: #23220 → #23227 → #23268 → this PR → #23229 → #23223 → #22307. #23229 builds the sequencer's separate seal and canonicalize steps on these helpers.

`rust-code-reviewer` and `deletion-reviewer` ran. The stale engine design doc they found is updated, and the Holocene fallback, which had no tests, now has them. Dismissed findings:
- Return `()` from `build_seal_and_insert`: the replacement's `L2BlockInfo` is now logged.
- Move the helpers into one module, or rename `synchronize/helper.rs`: each helper stays next to the task it came from.
- Rename `SynchronizeTaskError`: kept for API stability.
- Remove the unused `Metrics::FORKCHOICE_TASK_LABEL`: it was already unused before this PR.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Each retained helper commit compiles after restacking. The final stack passes 323 focused Rust tests, full Rust and Go lint, both validator and sequencer runtime suites, the restart suite, and conductor runtime coverage.
